snippet.title: I Built a Borehole Drilling rig for Ground Source Energy!
snippet.description:
I’m drilling a borehole to heat and cool my off-grid garden office using ground source energy — but at 4 metres down, I hit solid sandstone, and the DIY methods I’d used so far just couldn’t cut it.

Register & Get $70 new user coupons at JLCMC: https://jlcmc.com/?from=Battery 
Industrial Automation and Manufacturing-Focused Online Supply Chain at JLCMC
#jlcmc #jlcmcmechanicalparts

In a previous video, I built a basic airlift drilling system which made it through the soil and clay — but this rock layer brought everything to a halt. In this episode, I try several different techniques before finally building a 3.8m tall borehole rig with a 1HP motor, gearbox, and winch to help push deeper into the ground. My goal is to hit at least 12 metres for a functioning geothermal loop.

In the next video, I’ll be putting the finished rig to work and (hopefully!) drilling straight through the rock. You know when I purchased the drilling fluid from a company in the north of England he looked at me as if to say 'That will be harder than you realise'.

snippet.title: Off grid Cabin Build, Sheathing!  Part 4 in the series
snippet.description:
Sheathing a wood framed structure should be fun.  My kids got a kick out of nailing the panels on.  I'm using OSB, which stands for Oriented Strand Board, in 7/16" thickness.  The panels are spanning 2x8 framing members spaced 16 inches on center.  The footprint is 12 feet by 16 feet, which is just under 200 square feet.  The dimensions are nice because they are keeping to a 4 foot grid.  Since the sheathing panels are 4x8, this means there is almost no waste material.  

This off grid cabin will be insulated, heated, cooled, for a comfortable indoor environment year-round.  It will be powered with it's own solar system with panels and battery.
